propositions: Rebar must safely delegate authentication to provider-native SDKs and credential helpers rather than implementing a universal secret broker or generic get_secret() abstraction.

Operation snapshots must remain non-secret; provider-native pre-client credential capabilities (e.g., boto3 Session, Anthropic AccessTokenProvider, OpenAI workload identity) are injected into Rebar-owned factories, while unavoidable static credentials use provider-specific non-serializable SecretStr/SecretBytes containers excluded from serialization, caching, and fingerprints.

Static credential rotation for long-running processes is restart/redeploy based; Rebar does not poll environment, watch files, refresh SSM, or maintain hot-reload secret cache; short-lived CLI processes receive current startup environment; long-lived services require container restart to receive injected replacements.

Trusted same-capability child processes inherit ambient environment and native Git/SSH/AWS credential-process chains; Rebar overlays materialized static values only onto their owning child and removes only exact Rebar-declared sibling secret names; global os.environ is never mutated.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, vault, etc.) before process startup and supplies exactly one operation-certificate key via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (preferred) or multiline REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable; no application-owned SSM retrieval, universal broker, built-in keyring, or global allowlist is introduced.

All 17 application-sensitive inputs (provider auth, op-cert, Langfuse, observability, MCP, review-bot tokens) are classified as provider-owned, deployment-owned static adapter input, or Rebar-owned security material; operation snapshots, caches, fingerprints, tickets, MCP, CLI, and logs exclude secret values and credentials.
